display.title: Bitachon: Think Good and It Will Be Good
display.summary_short: After a painful attack in Eretz Yisroel, the storyteller teaches to ask 'for what?' instead of 'why?', and tells three stories showing how bitachon brings Hashem's blessing.
display.summary_long: The talk opens with a riddle: the same Hebrew letters can read 'lamah', why, or 'lemah', for what purpose. After a painful attack on Jews in Eretz Yisroel, asking why gets us nowhere; the Rebbe taught that our answer is to grow stronger, with more Torah, more mitzvos, more Ahavas Yisroel and above all simcha, which sweetens judgment, as the Alter Rebbe's smile at his trial showed. True bitachon is itself a source of blessing, as long as we also do our part. Three stories follow. The Tzemach Tzedek tells a worried father, 'Think good and it will be good', and his gravely ill son recovers at that very hour. Years later a Chassid near 770 receives the same words from the Rebbe when his father is in danger, with the same result. Finally the Baal Shem Tov shows his students an innkeeper who calmly farbrengs while the poritz's servant knocks three times for the rent he does not have, and on the road a buyer appears with exactly the money he needs.
display.lesson: Do your part and trust Hashem completely; thinking good brings good, and we answer hard times by growing stronger with joy.
